name: Ray Serve
supported_backends: none (orchestration layer - drives any Python callable)
supported_formats: passthrough (does not load weights - wraps Python callables)
notable_features: Framework-agnostic model serving - wraps any Python callable as a deployment
Model composition via DeploymentHandles - build complex inference pipelines in Python
Dynamic request batching for LLM workloads
Fractional GPUs - share GPU resources across deployments
Built on Ray core - scales to many machines
hardware_caveats: Python-only - no Go or Rust core
Fractional GPU sharing is not the same as MPS - it is Ray's own scheduling, not CUDA MPS
Model composition adds latency - each hop in the composition graph is a network call
Not Kubernetes-native - runs on Ray clusters, not K8s (though KubeRay provides a bridge)
Dynamic batching is per-deployment, not global - no cross-deployment batching
No built-in prefix-aware routing or KV cache management
best_for: Multi-model serving with complex composition (e.g., LLM + reranker + guardrail)
Teams already using Ray for training who want to use the same framework for serving
Python-heavy inference pipelines that need flexible composition
Fractional GPU sharing across many small models
avoid_for: Kubernetes-native deployments - Ray Serve is not K8s-native
Low-latency single-model serving where the composition overhead matters
Teams needing prefix-aware routing or KV cache management
notes: Ray Serve is a model serving library built on Ray. It is framework-agnostic and wraps any Python callable as a deployment. The key differentiator is model composition - you can build complex inference pipelines (LLM + reranker + guardrail) as a graph of deployments. Ray Serve supports dynamic request batching, multi-node/multi-GPU serving, and fractional GPU sharing. However, it is not Kubernetes-native (KubeRay provides a bridge), and it lacks LLM-specific features like prefix-aware routing and KV cache management. It is best suited for multi-model composition workloads rather than high-throughput single-model LLM serving.
